headline: IBM trains an AI model to build slide decks
dek: Palette has 20 billion parameters and follows a company's look, says IBM.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: Palette
body: IBM Research published Palette, an AI model that builds slide decks in the design language of whoever deploys it, per its post on Hugging Face.
It has 20 billion parameters, a fraction of frontier models (Hugging Face).

points.t: Decides the content and structure of each slide.
Writes code for position, width and font size.
Small enough to run on a company's own systems.

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: Faster
body: Because content is fixed before code, slides are generated in parallel, per IBM Research (Hugging Face).
On PresentBench, the model ranked first in two of three domains.

items.t: Accepts short commands across 12 categories (Hugging Face).
Keeping the model from inventing facts (Hugging Face).

caption.hook: IBM Research built Palette, an AI model for slide decks that follows a company's own look.
body: Per IBM Research on Hugging Face, Palette has 20 billion parameters and can run on a company's own infrastructure, which keeps confidential content away from third-party clouds. One role, the designer, decides each slide's content, and another, the coder, writes the code that places every element.

Because content is fixed before code, generation runs in parallel and gets 6 to 7 times faster. The team trained the model on about 1,000 synthetic decks and says it ranked first in two of three PresentBench domains. The hardest problem was keeping the model from inventing information.
